explanation: Hydrogen gas reduces black copper(II) oxide back to brown copper metal by removing its oxygen, while the hydrogen itself is oxidised to water.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: A black coating of copper(II) oxide powder, heated while hydrogen gas is passed over it.
beaker_view.final_appearance: The black coating turns to the reddish-brown colour of metallic copper.
beaker_view.observation: As hydrogen gas passes over the heated black powder, the colour visibly changes from black to reddish-brown copper, with droplets of water forming further along the tube.
